note: Rewritten from Silvestri's original description of 1914 (in Latin), published as Hoplognathotermes subterraneus sp. n., the type species of the genus Hoplognathotermes; besides the nymph, the soldier, the major and minor workers and measurements are included. The original uses a comma as the decimal separator; measurements have been transcribed as 10, 3.5, 2.5 and so on. The phrase 'Imago et miles ignota' in the text belongs to var. superior on the same page and not to this species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier large and thick-set; head about 1/4 longer than wide; mandibles slightly shorter than the head width, stout, tapering towards the apex and distinctly curved; left mandible with a large blunt basal tooth, right mandible with a pointed one. Antennae 15-segmented. The species is the type species of the genus Hoplognathotermes and differs clearly from the soldiers of Apicotermes in the shape of the head and the structure of the mandibles.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: body milk-straw coloured, head more or less pale ferruginous, the sides of the clypeus whitish, the apices of the mandibles black. Head large and thick, about 1/4 longer than wide, posterior corners broadly rounded, fairly convex upwards to the fontanelle, nearly flat in front, convex below, fontanelle very small. Labrum short, slightly wider than long, anterior margin sub-trapezoidal. Mandibles slightly shorter than the head width, stout, tapering towards the apex and distinctly curved, the tips acute; basal tooth of the left mandible large and blunt, that of the right mandible pointed. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 twice as long as segment 3, segment 4 about 1/4 longer than segment 3, segment 5 about 1/4 longer than segment 4. Anterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum slightly concave in the middle. Tibiae with few hairs, the apical spurs fairly stout; tarsal segments 1—3 slightly produced below at the apex. Tergites 1—9 of the abdomen with short to very short apical bristles, becoming more numerous posteriorly, tergite 10 with 3—4 rows of short or fairly long hairs; sternites with more numerous short hairs and short apical and anterior hairs; cerci short and thick. Measurements: body length 10 mm; head length 3.5 mm; head width 2.5 mm; antennal length 3.12 mm; mandible length 2.20 mm; pronotum width 1.56 mm; hind tibia length 2.58 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: body dirty ochraceous white or ochraceous, head yellow ferruginous or dirty ochraceous, the sides of the lower part of the head and the lateral and median areas behind the clypeus more or less chestnut, abdomen mouse-grey to black from the gut contents. Head nearly circular, with a few (4+4) hairs on the dorsum, fontanelle window pale, rather large and round, clypeus strongly inflated, half as long again as wide, with a median hair and two anterior hairs. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 about 3 times as long as segment 3, segment 3 about 1/4 longer than segment 4 and with a single outer hair, segment 5 nearly as long as segment 4. Anterior margin of the anterior lobe of the pronotum slightly or faintly concave in the middle. Legs slender and long, tibiae with fairly stout and numerous hairs and stout apical spurs, tarsal segments 1—3 produced very far below. Measurements: body length 6 mm; head width 1.58 mm; antennal length 2.64 mm; hind tibia length 2.08 mm. Minor worker: antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 about 2/3 longer than segment 3, segment 4 about 1/4 longer than segment 3. Measurements: body length 5.5 mm; head length 1.30 mm; head width 1.45 mm; antennal length 2.48 mm; hind tibia length 1.95 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Nymph: white, eyes black, antennae 16-segmented, segment 2 twice as long as segment 3, segments 3 and 4 subequal, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4; body length 9 mm, wing pads 1.4 mm long. Localities: Conakry, Camayenne and Kakoulima, French Guinea; a few specimens were taken three times in galleries under stones or about 20 cm deep in the soil; no nest was found, which should be subterranean.
